players.product: merchant semiconductor photomasks (binary, phase-shift, EUV) and nanoimprint molds (formerly Toppan Photomask; TSE Prime listing Oct 2025; TOPPAN Holdings holds 46.55%)

quarterly_data.quarter: Tekscend Photomask annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 (April 2025 - March 2026) results, single photomask segment: revenue JPY 129,576 million, up 9.8%; operating profit JPY 27,530 million, down 2.4%, as higher material costs and depreciation plus one-off listing-related costs weighed, so the operating margin fell to 21.2% (23.9% a year earlier); profit before tax JPY 33,432 million, up 8.6%; profit attributable to owners of the parent JPY 24,947 million, up 150.9%. Company-defined adjusted operating profit was JPY 28,407 million and adjusted EBITDA JPY 47,444 million. Production roughly equals sales because lead times are short, and the company does not disclose orders received for the same reason.
quarterly_data.figure: Revenue JPY 129,576 million (+9.8%); operating profit JPY 27,530 million (-2.4%), margin 21.2%; adjusted EBITDA JPY 47,444 million

quarterly_data.quarter: Tekscend Photomask annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management states that, with data-center investment driven by generative AI and cloud demand staying high, photomask demand was firm at every node from leading-edge to mature: leading-edge demand for high-precision, high-value masks stayed strong with a stable order environment, and mature-process demand held up across a wide range of applications. In the merchant (external) photomask market, outsourcing demand grew from foundries that do not make their own masks, and IDMs that make masks in-house also outsourced more because of internal resource shortages. Logic photomasks are the company's main product, but external demand for memory photomasks is also rising on HBM development competition, growing memory demand and tight memory supply capacity.

quarterly_data.quarter: Tekscend Photomask annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The company states it was the top merchant photomask maker for semiconductors in 2024 with a 37.8% share of that market (citing SEMI's 2024 Photomask Characterization Study). It produces photomasks at 8 plants (5 in Asia, 1 in the US, 2 in Europe); Singapore currently performs only data processing, with a new plant scheduled to start operating during fiscal year 2026 (the report's own wording, stated as a future start). Required delivery after receiving customer pattern data is typically about 2 weeks even for leading-edge masks and 2-3 days for legacy masks, so plants sit near customers and plants back each other up through intra-group production outsourcing.
quarterly_data.figure: 37.8% share of the 2024 merchant semiconductor photomask market (SEMI); 8 plants

quarterly_data.quarter: Tekscend Photomask annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Capex plan for the year after March 2026 totals JPY 63,000 million: growth investment JPY 48,500 million (building new plants in Singapore and Korea and adding manufacturing equipment in the US and elsewhere), legacy investment JPY 6,000 million (replacing aging equipment) and other JPY 8,500 million (strengthening related systems). FY2026 capex, including intangibles, was JPY 33,236 million, mainly EUV mask production equipment led by multi-beam mask writers, plus legacy tool replacement and life extension.
quarterly_data.figure: Capex plan JPY 63,000 million (growth JPY 48,500 million); FY2026 capex JPY 33,236 million

quarterly_data.quarter: Tekscend Photomask annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: New plants: the company is building a new plant in Singapore to capture growth in Southeast Asia and India, citing government support that is concentrating semiconductor production there, proximity to major customers and its strategic value as a future supply base for the Indian market. It also plans a third plant in Korea to further strengthen supply there and ensure stable supply, citing rising photomask demand in leading-edge semiconductors on AI and data-center growth.
quarterly_data.figure: New Singapore plant under construction; third Korea plant planned; no specific figure

quarterly_data.quarter: Tekscend Photomask annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Strategy (management states): capacity-expansion capex will prioritize the US and Asian countries other than China, where volume demand is expected to grow; in China, where US-China decoupling and the government's localization policy have intensified competition with local rivals, the company will pursue selective business and capex focused on profitability. It considers it important, in every region, to build stable relationships with local authorities and through long-term supply agreements with leading customers. For legacy nodes it is replacing legacy tools under a group-wide renewal plan and extending tool life, including co-developing substitute parts with third-party vendors.

quarterly_data.quarter: Tekscend Photomask annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Leading-edge technology: the company has installed multi-beam mask writers at its Asaka and Dresden plants and started EUV mask development and production, and is applying curvilinear and other latest technologies to optical-mask production. In EUV it is developing new blanks for High-NA lithography with a blanks maker and aims to lead competitors in next-generation EUV masks. R&D in FY2026: it built a mask process for a new EUV absorber material co-developed with a blanks maker and, with imec and IBM, ran wafer exposure tests that confirmed good characteristics on the wafer; it also developed next-generation mask inspection functions with an equipment maker. R&D expense was JPY 1,238 million, centered on the Asaka plant and the equity-method affiliate AMTC.

quarterly_data.quarter: Tekscend Photomask annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Material contract: a Joint Research and Development Agreement with IBM, signed January 25, 2024, for joint R&D for 5 years from February 2024 on photomasks for the 2nm logic process node using EUV lithography, including High-NA EUV.
quarterly_data.figure: 5-year joint R&D from February 2024 (2nm, EUV / High-NA EUV)

quarterly_data.quarter: Tekscend Photomask annual securities report: FY2026 (06-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: New business: using nanoimprint lithography, the company is commercializing master molds for AR-glass waveguides, adding 3D-structure (slanted and blazed) master molds to binary ones, and is setting up 3D master-mold production in Japan and Europe. It has also built a prototype line at the Asaka plant as the core of a planned nanoimprint contract-processing service in Japan, aimed at optical parts such as AR glasses and metalenses, and is preparing for volume production.

contracts.signal: Material contract: a Joint Venture Agreement between Tekscend Photomask US Inc. (formerly Toppan Photomasks Inc.) and GLOBALFOUNDRIES MANAGEMENT SERVICES LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY & CO. KG (parent: GlobalFoundries Inc.), signed January 15, 2010, to run Advanced Mask Technology Center GmbH & Co. KG (AMTC) as a joint venture. AMTC's production capacity is used 70% by GlobalFoundries and 30% by Tekscend Photomask US, which secures the group's photomask supply capacity in Europe, including leading-edge masks. It remains in force as long as the three-party Limited Partnership Agreement does, which runs indefinitely unless a party gives notice to end the partnership.
